issues.description: Behavior change: s.state[k]=sorted now only runs when yield returns true, with no comment or test justifying the new postcondition.
issues.detail: Previously the sorted marker was set unconditionally after pop; now it only fires on yield success. The deferred clear(s.state) papers over this on reuse, but the invariant is implicit and coupled across distant lines. State the postcondition explicitly so the next maintainer does not silently break it.

issues.description: Moving cleanup into defer entangles iterator lifetime with Sorter reset and hides the entry precondition.
issues.detail: The original entry-time clear was a defensive reset; the new defer-based reset only runs if the returned iter.Seq is actually invoked. If Sort() is called and never iterated, prior state persists. Either restore an explicit entry precondition or document the reuse invariant clearly.

issues.description: State machine collapse from working/walking to a single label is undocumented and lacks a stated invariant.
issues.detail: Merging 'working' and 'walking' into one state is plausibly correct, but push()'s cycle-detection branch now reuses the label for two distinct temporal phases. No invariant distinguishes first from second visit, and no termination argument is given. Add a comment stating the invariant and why one state suffices.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR's stated purpose is fixing state reuse across Sort() calls, but no test calling Sort() twice on the same Sorter is included. Without a regression test, the next refactor will silently reintroduce the bug. Add a Sort()-twice test that demonstrates the original failure.

issues.description: Three independent changes squashed into one diff hurts bisect and review.
issues.detail: The patch combines (1) collapsing working/walking, (2) fixing s.stack[0:] no-op with clear()+[:0], and (3) moving sorted-marker inside the yield branch. Each is a distinct bug with distinct reasoning. Split into separate commits so bisect works and each change carries its own justification.

issues.description: Comment rewrite contains typos ('visisted', 'if its') in the now load-bearing state-machine explanation.
issues.detail: Since the state machine just lost a state, this comment is the canonical description of the two-visit DFS model. 'visisted' should be 'visited' and 'if its' should be 'if it's'. Clean up the prose in a correctness-critical comment.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying simplifications are sound — collapsing working/walking is correct taste, and the s.stack[0:] no-op fix is a real bug squashed. But the PR is presented as a correctness fix without the discipline that demands: no stated invariant or termination argument, a subtle behavioral change to when sorted is marked on early yield termination, and cleanup moved into defer that entangles iterator lifetime with Sorter reset. Three independent fixes are squashed into one diff, no regression test demonstrates the state-reuse bug, and the load-bearing comment has typos. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — split the patches, add a Sort()-twice regression test, state the reuse invariant, and clean the comment before merging.
